newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka detains eight refugee traffickers.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka detains eight refugee traffickers.

text.p: Sri Lanka has detained eight men believed to be Indian nationals for allegedly collaborating with separatist Tamil rebels to ferry refugees to India, a navy spokesman said on Saturday.
The men were taken into custody after a navy gunboat destroyed their trawler in the Gulf of Mannar Sea off northern Sri Lanka late on Thursday night, the spokesman told Reuters.
"We are pretty sure they are Indian nationals, although they had no identity papers with them. We are making checks with Indian authorities in Colombo," he said.
Indian high commission officials were not immediately available for comment.
The spokesman said the men, now in police custody, were believed to be involved in an operation by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) to ferry minority Tamil refugees to southern India.
The LTTE, fighting for an independent homeland in this predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island, say thousands of Tamils have been made homeless by the war, now in its 14th year.
In February, at least 130 people drowned when a trawler carrying some 150 Tamil refugees to India capsized in waters off Mannar town, 240 km (150 miles) north of Colombo.
The Tigers said the refugees were fleeing a military offensive to capture a highway linking Mannar with the government-controlled northern town of Vavuniya, about 80 km (50 miles) east of Mannar.
The spokesman said one of the men had a letter allegedly issued by the LTTE authorising the men to take 40,000 rupees ($700) for services rendered to the rebel organisation.
But except for 100 rupees in Indian currency, no other money was found on them, he added.
